name: Joiarib
overview: Joiarib was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Zechariah. His mention in Nehemiah 11:5 situates him within the post-exilic community of Israel. Beyond his paternal lineage, Scripture provides no additional personal details or notable events concerning him.
namesAndTitles: The name Joiarib means 'YHWH contends' or 'pleads your case,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, was not given directly by God but carries the significance of divine advocacy or contention.
familyAndRelationships: Joiarib is explicitly identified as the son of Zechariah and is inferred to be the father of Adaiah, according to Nehemiah 11:5. These relationships place him within a familial line in the tribe of Judah, though no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: While Joiarib's role in the biblical narrative is limited, his inclusion in the genealogical record of Nehemiah 11:5 underscores the faithfulness and continuity of the post-exilic community of Judah. His identification as the son of Zechariah links him to the restoration period, highlighting the generational preservation of the covenant people. Thus, Joiarib serves as a testament to God's ongoing work in preserving His chosen lineage.
